title: Block first, mix after a later retest
statement: Practise a new skill on its own while it is being learned, and mix it into review only after it passes a retest on new items on a later day.
example: A skill becomes eligible for mixing only after a retest at least 24 hours later on new parallel items.
detail: The reading project's practice spec keeps a skill in blocked practice while it is being acquired and makes it eligible for interleaving only after a delayed (≥24h) retest passed on new parallel items; completion on the day of release never qualifies, because same-day testing measures working memory, not learning (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). The course standard draws the same boundary, introducing interleaving only after prerequisite acquisition is secure and listing same-day success called durable as a failure signal (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, Q024). In mixed review, no two items in a row are on the same skill.
against: The Grade 3 criteria differ on the stage: one row admits an item to mixed review after the delayed retest, another interleaves only after the later mastery stage (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D6-practice-durable-mastery.md`, D6.6 and D6.7). These are design rules, not results: nothing here measured the effect of the order, and the course graph is a draft pending rulings (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0122-g3-reading-course-graph.qmd`).

evidence.quote: **Interleaving eligibility = E2-cleared**: a delayed (≥24h) retest passed on *new* parallel items — release-day completion never qualifies
